data.hypothesis: A two-group scalar unroll may expose independent table-lookup chains and amortize loop control compared with the measured scalar baseline (three samples, mean 55.0005 µs), while preserving the original one-group path for tails and invalid input. Register pressure and added control may negate any benefit; no speedup is assumed.
data.notes: Submitted one two-group scalar candidate; no alternate group sizes or unsuccessful choices were timed in this action. No commands or tests were run here, so empty/short inputs, unroll-boundary lengths, padding variants, random inputs, Lena, and repeated native timing remain for controller validation. The baseline was correct on 10 recorded cases; its measured mean was 55.0005 µs.
transformations: Unrolled the safe decode loop by two eight-character groups when at least 21 input bytes remain, loading and looking up both groups before committing output.

Preserved fallback semantics: if the first group is invalid, leave it for bytewise processing; if only the second is invalid, commit the first group and resume at the second. Retained the original single-group loop for remaining safe blocks.
Used scalar operations only; did not add SIMD, threading, or benchmark-size specialization.
